Nopers! MV tilesets are 48x48 pixels. You can totally use plugins to use any tile size you want to, but it makes it harder to work with.
RPG Maker MZ can work with different sized tilesets right in the editor, including 16x16. It still makes the UI and camera a biiiiit wonky sometimes, so you might consider resizing up to 32x32 - but it works-nyan!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Nyro17 said:
performance for android users
Click to expand...
So, I can't say for sure since I don't bother with mobile games, however, I think MZ might be the better option here.
Technically, there are plugins for MV to allow for smaller tile sizes, but it's sort of a hacky-solution of having a 16x16 version of your tileset (the one that is used in the actual game) and a 48x48 version (used so you can see wtf you are doing in the actual editor).
In one of the MZ updates (I think it was 1.5) they natively added the ability change what your tilesize is. So for sure, I'd say MZ is your better option here. Of course, I've heard that no matter what you pick, it can be a real chore to package your deployed game into an APK file that can actually run on an Android device. Part of the challenge being is that...well...a lot of us just don't do it, so if something breaks there's also very limited existing support and knowledge base on how to fix problems. It's sort of a frontier you'll have to figure out for yourself.
That being said, neither engine has an elegant solution for screen scaling; no vector graphics support or internal render-resolution with an upscaler. This can cause problems since mobile devices tend to have a wide range of display sizes and resolutions, with cheap android devices today still shipping with 720 or 1080p screen. Meanwhile some flagship devices have 9:16 screens, 9:21 screens, some 9:23 screens, and then we get into the world of foldable devices were we deal with some 1:1 or 4:3 sized screens when unfolded, and when folder - like in the case of Galazy devices - some really narrow screen ratios.
As for performance itself, once again, I cannot say for sure. MZ again is probably a better option since it supports 64x OS. MV only support 32x OS and as a result can only take advantage of a menial amount of RAM. Neither engine, however, takes full advantage of multi-core CPUs or GPUs, and instead prefer single cores that are clocked high. iirc, modern mobile chips often opt for many small efficient cores, rather than a few power-hungry cores so multi-threading is preferred on mobile devices, so performance for MV/MZ games may take a hit there. This all depends on how much parallel processing you use in your game, and the type of complicated plugins and effects you are running.

As for all the other questions, the entire code to the engine's logic is available to be edited and modified as you see fit.
However, the editor itself cannot be modified.
Enabling these solutions would require skill on your part, not just understanding JS, but also how to use the engine.
As I said in my April Fools response, changing engines is a serious undertaking that you really should reconsider.
If you are wanting more robust online features, I really think RPG Maker is the wrong choice. Consider Unity or Unreal.

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body:
From what I've read here, I'd recommend against switching engines. Android support and multiplayer are both technically possible in RM, but both are really difficult not something remotely possible within just the engine itself.
Android exporting requires a fair amount of work in Android Studio and probably fixing up plugins that will inevitably break there. Multiplayer requires complicated plugins to enable, and even with those tends to rather unreliable.
Moving a multiplayer mobile game from an engine that can make them to one that can't won't really help you, if anything your performance issues would likely get worse.
